28921565.title: The impact of P-glycoprotein and breast cancer resistance protein on the brain pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of a panel of MEK inhibitors

SELUMETINIB: Interestingly, neither single knockout mouse strain demonstrated any increased brain penetration, indicative of redundancy between P-gp and BCRP as has been observed for various other compounds. The brain-to-plasma ratio was only about 0.02, which is close to the fraction of blood in brain
The selumetinib brain-to-plasma ratio increased in Abcb1a/b;Abcg2-/- mice, but remained very poor (0.06).
Whereas plasma levels were similar in wildtype and transporter knockout mice, the brain concentration of selumetinib was 3.5-fold increased in Abcb1a/b;Abcg2-/- mice following i.v. administration.

Based on our preclinical data, we demonstrate that brain access of selumetinib is efficiently restricted (brain-to-plasma ratio of only 0.02-0.06) and results in just a marginal inhibition of intracranial MEK at clinically achievable plasma concentrations.
Notably, target inhibition could also be demonstrated for selumetinib, but only at plasma levels far above levels in patients receiving the maximum tolerated dose.
BINIMETINIB: PD0325901 displayed more promising characteristics than trametinib (GSK1120212), binimetinib (MEK162), selumetinib (AZD6244), and pimasertib (AS703026): PD0325901 was the weakest substrate of P-gp and BCRP in vitro, its brain penetration was only marginally higher in Abcb1a/b;Abcg2-/- mice, and efficient target inhibition in the brain could be achieved at clinically relevant plasma levels.
Our study investigates five MEK inhibitors that are in clinical development: pimasertib (AS703026), PD0325901, binimetinib (MEK162), selumetinib (AZD6244), and trametinib (GSK1120212).

Samples were analyzed using an LC-MS/MS method as described for trametinib and binimetinib CETAs. [Note: the in vivo brain pharmacokinetic experiments in this paper cover PD0325901, selumetinib and pimasertib only; binimetinib appears in the in vitro transport assays and the comparative summary.]
